regulatory_bodies.name: Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation
regulatory_bodies.description: Russia's Ministry of Health sets pharmaceutical policy. Roszdravnadzor enforces drug registration. Russia applies EAEU (Eurasian Economic Union) technical regulations for drugs and devices in common with Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan.

regulatory_bodies.name: Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance Russia
regulatory_bodies.description: Russia's agricultural product safety surveillance body. Together with Rospotrebnadzor, enforces food safety at Russia's borders and within the EAEU.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministry of Health Poland — Drug Policy Department
regulatory_bodies.description: Poland's Ministry of Health (and URPL — Office for Registration of Medicinal Products) implements EU pharmaceutical regulations as an EU member state. Polish NCA for EMA procedures.

regulatory_bodies.name: Office for Registration of Medicinal Products Medical Devices and Biocidal Products Poland
regulatory_bodies.description: Poland's medicine and device registration office. Applies EU pharmaceutical Directives and MDR/IVDR as EU member state. One of the larger EU NCAs by volume of applications.

regulatory_bodies.name: Chief Sanitary Inspectorate Poland
regulatory_bodies.description: Poland's chief sanitary inspectorate enforces EU food law, food supplements regulation, and conducts market surveillance.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministry of Public Health Qatar
regulatory_bodies.description: Qatar's comprehensive public health ministry. MOPH regulates pharmaceuticals, food safety, and medical devices. Strong institutional capacity with significant investment in regulatory infrastructure.

regulatory_bodies.name: Gulf Standards Organisation
regulatory_bodies.description: GCC-wide standards body issuing Gulf Standards (GSO/UAE.S) for food products. Standards are mandatory across all 6 GCC countries: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman.

regulatory_bodies.name: National Health Regulatory Authority Bahrain
regulatory_bodies.description: Bahrain's comprehensive health regulatory authority. GCC pharmaceutical harmonised track applies. NHRA is modern and internationally oriented.

regulatory_bodies.name: Directorate of Pharmacy and Drug Control Oman
regulatory_bodies.description: Oman's pharmaceutical and health product regulator. GCC harmonisation applies for pharmaceuticals. MOCIPH (Ministry of Commerce) regulates food.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministry of Health Kuwait
regulatory_bodies.description: Kuwait MOH regulates pharmaceuticals and food. GCC pharmaceutical registration track. Food standards by PAFN (Public Authority for Food and Nutrition).

regulatory_bodies.name: Public Authority for Food and Nutrition Kuwait
regulatory_bodies.description: Kuwait's public authority for food and nutrition sets food standards and regulates food imports. GSO standards apply.

regulatory_bodies.name: Jordan Food and Drug Administration
regulatory_bodies.description: One of the most progressive regulators in the Arab region. JFDA issues comprehensive regulatory guidance. Jordan serves as a regional registration hub for MENA markets.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministry of Public Health Lebanon
regulatory_bodies.description: Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health regulates pharmaceuticals and food. Significant economic challenges since 2019 have impacted regulatory capacity but the framework remains based on solid French-influenced legislation.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministry of Health Iraq
regulatory_bodies.description: Iraq's Ministry of Health issues pharmaceutical registrations. Regulatory capacity rebuilding post-2003. Many imported products registered via Gulf countries first.

regulatory_bodies.name: Iran Food and Drug Administration
regulatory_bodies.description: Iran's national food and drug administration under the Ministry of Health. Regulates pharmaceuticals, food, cosmetics, and medical devices. Domestic pharmaceutical production is significant. Import registration is restricted by sanctions environment.

regulatory_bodies.name: National Food Protection and Safety Monitoring Department Algeria
regulatory_bodies.description: Algeria's food safety regulatory body under the Ministry of Health. Food additives and contaminant limits largely follow EU regulations due to strong trade ties.

regulatory_bodies.name: Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament Tunisia
regulatory_bodies.description: Tunisia's pharmaceutical directorate. Issues marketing authorisations. Tunisia has bilateral pharmaceutical agreements with EU countries.

regulatory_bodies.name: Office National de Sécurité Sanitaire des Produits Alimentaires Morocco
regulatory_bodies.description: Morocco's comprehensive food safety authority. Aligns food standards with EU due to Association Agreement and Advanced Status. Strong institutional capacity.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministry of Public Health Morocco — DMPCI
regulatory_bodies.description: Morocco's pharmaceutical and health product regulatory directorate. Issues marketing authorisations. Alignment with EU pharmaceutical law ongoing under Association Agreement.

regulatory_bodies.name: Service de Documentation et des Statistiques de la Pharmacie Cameroon
regulatory_bodies.description: Cameroon's pharmaceutical service under the Ministry of Public Health. Issues import authorisations and marketing approvals. CEMAC (Central African Economic Community) harmonisation in progress.

regulatory_bodies.name: Rwanda Biomedical Centre — Regulatory
regulatory_bodies.description: Rwanda's pharmaceutical and health product regulator, recently strengthened. Rwanda implements East African Community (EAC) pharmaceutical harmonisation. Strong governance capacity.

regulatory_bodies.name: Medicines Control Authority of Zimbabwe
regulatory_bodies.description: Zimbabwe's medicines control authority. Issues marketing licences. Member of ZAZIBONA (Zambia, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Namibia) mutual recognition scheme.

regulatory_bodies.name: Zambia Medicines Regulatory Authority
regulatory_bodies.description: Zambia's pharmaceutical and medical device regulator. Member of ZAZIBONA harmonisation scheme. Growing institutional capacity.

regulatory_bodies.name: Instituto Nacional de Fiscalização de Alimentos, Medicamentos Angola
regulatory_bodies.description: Angola's food and pharmaceutical regulatory institute. Portuguese-speaking country with significant Brazilian trade ties. Regulatory framework influenced by Portuguese pharmaceutical law.

regulatory_bodies.name: National Drug Authority Uganda
regulatory_bodies.description: Uganda's pharmaceutical and health product regulator under the NDA Act Cap 206. EAC harmonisation member. One of the more active African regulators.

regulatory_bodies.name: Tanzania Food and Drugs Authority
regulatory_bodies.description: Tanzania's comprehensive food and drugs authority. TFDA Act 2003 governs. EAC harmonisation member. Growing regional registration hub role.

licensing_pathways.license_type: State Registration — Биологически Активная Добавка (BAD / Biologically Active Dietary Supplement)
licensing_pathways.competent_authority: Rospotrebnadzor (Federal Service for Surveillance on Consumer Rights) + Roszdravnadzor
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as BAD (Биологически Активная Добавка) under TR TS 021/2011 (EAEU Technical Regulation on Food Safety)
2. Product must comply with EAEU TR TS 021/2011 and SanPiN 2.3.2.1290-03 (BAD-specific requirements)
3. Obtain safety assessment and hygienic evaluation from Rospotrebnadzor-accredited laboratory
4. Appoint Russian legal entity / registered importer
5. Submit State Registration dossier to Rospotrebnadzor
6. Rospotrebnadzor review and issuance of State Registration Certificate (Свидетельство о государственной регистрации)
7. Product registered in unified EAEU register — valid across Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan
8. Russian-language label mandatory with State Registration number
9. Halal/Kosher certification commercially important but not legally mandatory
prerequisites: All ingredients on EAEU permitted list for BADs

gmp_requirements.standard: GOST R 52249 (GMP for food supplements, based on WHO GMP)
gmp_requirements.eaeu: TR TS 025/2012 and TR TS 022/2011 requirements

renewal_requirements: No fixed renewal — State Registration Certificate is indefinite unless formula changed
licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: TR TS 021/2011 (EAEU Food Safety Technical Regulation); TR TS 022/2011 (EAEU Food Labelling); SanPiN 2.3.2.1290-03 (BAD requirements); Federal Law No. 29-FZ (Food Safety)
licensing_pathways.notes: EAEU registration is highly valuable — one registration covers 5 countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia, and Kyrgyzstan (combined population ~185 million). The EAEU regulatory framework is increasingly harmonised with Codex and EU standards, but has unique requirements. Western sanctions (post-2022) may affect logistics and payment for some companies.

licensing_pathways.license_type: Notification to Chief Sanitary Inspectorate (GIS) — Suplement Diety
licensing_pathways.competent_authority: Chief Sanitary Inspectorate (GIS) + EU NCA for pharmaceutical/device matters
pathway_steps: 1. As EU member, Poland applies EU Directive 2002/46/EC and EU Regulation 1169/2011 (FIC)
2. Verify all ingredients on EU permitted vitamins/minerals list (Directive 2002/46/EC)
3. Notify GIS (Główny Inspektorat Sanitarny) via notification portal before first placement on Polish market
4. Notification requires: product name, formulation, label specimen, contact details
5. GIS acknowledges notification — no pre-market approval review
6. Polish-language label mandatory (meeting EU FIC requirements)
7. For novel ingredients: EU Novel Food authorisation from EFSA required (as for all EU markets)
prerequisites: EU Directive 2002/46/EC compliant ingredients and doses
licensing_pathways.fast_track_details: EU harmonised system — notify GIS and market immediately for standard permitted ingredients.

gmp_requirements.standard: EU GMP for food supplements; HACCP mandatory under Regulation 852/2004

post_approval_obligations: Report food safety incidents per EU rapid alert system (RASFF)
licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: EU Directive 2002/46/EC; EU Regulation 1169/2011 (FIC); Polish Food Safety Act (Ustawa o bezpieczeństwie żywności i żywienia) 2006
licensing_pathways.notes: Poland is a major EU market and distribution hub for Central/Eastern Europe. EU harmonisation means that products compliant for any EU member state are generally marketable in Poland. Polish label and GIS notification are the only country-specific requirements.

licensing_pathways.license_type: Product Registration — MOPH Qatar / GCC Harmonised Track
licensing_pathways.competent_authority: Ministry of Public Health Qatar (MOPH) + GSO (Gulf Standards Organisation)
pathway_steps: 1. Appoint Qatar registered agent/importer
2. Verify product complies with GSO standards for food supplements and GCC positive ingredient list
3. Obtain Halal certification from Qatar-recognized body
4. Prepare registration dossier: formulation, CoA, safety data, label
5. Submit via MOPH online registration system
6. MOPH review: typically 60–120 days
7. GCC track: if already registered in Saudi Arabia or UAE, Gulf Cooperation certificate accepted
8. Receive Qatar registration number
9. Arabic-English bilingual label mandatory
licensing_pathways.fast_track_details: GCC mutual recognition: products registered in Saudi Arabia (SFDA) or UAE may receive faster review in Qatar.

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP equivalent required (WHO-GMP or reference country GMP)

licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Qatar Food Safety Law No. 8 of 2010; GSO food supplement standards; Qatar Cabinet Resolution No. 13/2020
licensing_pathways.notes: Qatar is a high-income market with high consumer purchasing power. Halal compliance is essential — Qatar is a Muslim-majority country. The FIFA World Cup 2022 significantly boosted Qatar's food safety regulatory investment.

pathway_steps: 1. Classify as dietary supplement under Jordan Food and Drug Law No. 31 of 2018
2. Appoint Jordanian registered agent
3. Verify all ingredients comply with JFDA permitted list for food supplements
4. Prepare CTD-aligned dossier
5. Submit registration application via JFDA online portal
6. JFDA review: typically 60–90 working days
7. Receive Registration Certificate
8. Arabic-English bilingual label
9. Jordan is a regional hub — registration often used as stepping stone to other Arab markets
licensing_pathways.fast_track_details: JFDA has an expedited review for products from reference regulatory authorities (FDA, EMA, TGA, HC).
licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Food and Drug Law No. 31 of 2018; JFDA dietary supplement guidelines
licensing_pathways.notes: Jordan is an important MENA hub. JFDA registration is often used by international companies as a reference registration for other Arab markets (Iraq, Libya, Yemen, Lebanon). Jordan has bilateral pharmaceutical mutual recognition discussions with EU.

licensing_pathways.license_type: Autorisation de Mise sur le Marché (AMM) or ONSSA notification
licensing_pathways.competent_authority: ONSSA (Office National de Sécurité Sanitaire des Produits Alimentaires) for food supplements
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as complément alimentaire (food supplement) — regulated as food under Loi 28-07
2. Appoint Moroccan importer/distributor
3. Verify formulation complies with Decree No. 2-12-502 on food supplements
4. Prepare registration dossier: formulation, CoA, label, safety evidence
5. Submit to ONSSA for food supplements; Ministry of Health (DMPCI) for products with medicinal claims
6. ONSSA review and approval
7. Receive ONSSA authorization number
8. French and Arabic bilingual label mandatory

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per Moroccan ONSSA requirements; EU-equivalent GMP accepted

licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Loi 28-07 relative à la sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires; Décret 2-12-502 (Compléments Alimentaires 2013)
licensing_pathways.notes: Morocco has an EU Association Agreement (Accord d'Association) creating strong alignment with EU food law. Products with EU approvals receive smoother ONSSA review. French is the de facto language of business and regulation alongside Arabic. Morocco is a gateway to Francophone West Africa.

pathway_steps: 1. Appoint Bahrain registered agent
2. GCC Track: if product is already registered in Saudi Arabia (SFDA) — submit via GCC mutual recognition pathway
3. For new registration: prepare GSO-compliant dossier with Halal certificate
4. Submit via NHRA online system
5. NHRA review: 30–60 days for GCC track products
6. Receive NHRA registration number
7. Arabic-English bilingual label
documents_required: Free Sale Certificate or GCC registration
licensing_pathways.fast_track_details: GCC mutual recognition: Saudi SFDA or UAE registration significantly accelerates NHRA review.

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP equivalent per WHO or reference country

renewal_requirements: Annual registration fee; renewal before expiry
licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Bahrain Health Services Law; GSO standards; GCC Pharmaceutical harmonisation framework
licensing_pathways.notes: Bahrain's NHRA is one of the most responsive and modern regulators in the GCC. The GCC mutual recognition track significantly reduces registration burden if product is already registered in Saudi Arabia or UAE.

pathway_steps: 1. Classify as health supplement under FDA Act 851 of 2012
2. Appoint Ghanaian local agent
3. Herbal medicines: classified separately under Traditional Herbal Medicine (THM) category
4. Prepare dossier: formulation, CoA, safety and efficacy data, label
5. Submit registration application to FDA-Ghana
6. FDA-Ghana technical review and laboratory testing
7. Site inspection for domestic manufacturers
8. Receive FDA-Ghana Registration Number
9. English-language label (Ghana's official language) with FDA-Ghana number
renewal_requirements: Apply before expiry; product retesting may be required
licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Food and Drugs Authority Act 851 of 2012 (Ghana); FDA-Ghana Food Supplement Guidelines
licensing_pathways.notes: Ghana is an increasingly important West African market. FDA-Ghana has been strengthening its framework with WHO support. The ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) pharmaceutical harmonisation scheme (ECOWAS/MHN/RA/2016) may eventually allow regional mutual recognition.

pathway_steps: 1. Classify drug category under Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics Act 2003
2. Appoint Tanzanian registered agent/distributor
3. WHO-PQ or reference country approval strongly preferred
4. Prepare CTD-format dossier
5. Submit application to TFDA
6. TFDA review: priority review for WHO-prequalified products
7. Laboratory testing by TFDA National Quality Control Laboratory
8. Receive Marketing Authorization Certificate
9. Swahili and English bilingual label
licensing_pathways.fast_track_details: WHO-prequalified products receive priority review at TFDA. EAC (East African Community) harmonisation may enable streamlined review.

gmp_requirements.inspection: TFDA may conduct overseas inspection for new manufacturers

licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics Act 2003; TFDA Drug Registration Guidelines; EAC Drug Registration Harmonisation Guidelines
licensing_pathways.notes: Tanzania is an EAC member implementing the EAC pharmaceutical harmonisation scheme. EAC harmonisation (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan) is progressing — mutual recognition may significantly reduce registration costs in the region.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: TR TS 021/2011 (EAEU Technical Regulation on Food Safety) — Appendix 3 Contaminants
allowable_limits.notes: EAEU (Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan) applies unified TR TS 021/2011 contaminant limits. Limits are broadly aligned with Codex but some differ.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: EU Commission Regulation 2023/915 amending 1881/2006 (applies in Poland as EU member)
allowable_limits.notes: Poland applies EU contaminant limits. As EU member state, all EU food safety regulations apply directly.
EAEU applies 2 μg/kg AFB1 limit for cereals — same as EU. Russia is a major grain exporter; mycotoxin control is commercially critical.
Morocco's aflatoxin limits are stricter than Codex (10 μg/kg) for groundnuts due to EU export requirements. Morocco aligns with EU standards for export-oriented products.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: TR TS 029/2012 (EAEU Technical Regulation on Food Additives Safety)
allowable_limits.notes: EAEU TR TS 029/2012 governs food additives across all 5 member states. Limits generally align with Codex GSFA.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: EU Regulation 1333/2008 (applies in Poland as EU member state)
allowable_limits.notes: Poland applies EU additive regulations. Stricter EU limit of 150 mg/L applies for beverages (vs Codex/US 600–1000 mg/kg).

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: TR TS 029/2012 (EAEU Food Additives Technical Regulation)
allowable_limits.notes: EAEU permits tartrazine at Codex-aligned limits. Russia uses EAEU additive numbering (E-number system).
EAEU TR TS 021/2011 Appendix 1 sets comprehensive microbiological limits. Zero tolerance for Salmonella in all food products.
Qatar applies GSO microbiological standards. Dubai Municipality-style active port surveillance testing of imported foods.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: TR TS 022/2011 (EAEU Food Labelling Technical Regulation) — Annex 1 NRVs
allowable_limits.notes: EAEU NRV for Vitamin C: 70 mg/day (lower than EU 80 mg; lower than US 90 mg). Used for % NRV labelling in Russia/EAEU.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: TR TS 022/2011 (EAEU Food Labelling) — NRV Annex
allowable_limits.notes: EAEU NRV for sodium: 2000 mg/day. EAEU food labelling requires % NRV based on TR TS 022/2011 table.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: TR TS 021/2011 — Contaminants in Fishery Products (EAEU)
allowable_limits.notes: EAEU mercury limit for non-predatory fish: 0.5 mg/kg; for predatory species (tuna, swordfish): 1.0 mg/kg.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: Hygienic Standards GN 1.2.3111-13 — MRLs for Pesticides (Russia)
allowable_limits.notes: Russia sets MRLs via its own Hygienic Standards GN system. Some MRLs differ from EU and Codex. Russia is the world's largest wheat exporter — glyphosate MRLs in wheat are commercially significant.
Russia MRL for chlorpyrifos in vegetables: 0.3 mg/kg — more permissive than EU (0.01 mg/kg default after EU ban) but stricter than some markets.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: SanPiN 2.3.2.1290-03 — Hygienic Requirements for BADs (Dietary Supplements)
allowable_limits.notes: Russia's SanPiN 2.3.2.1290-03 sets specific microbiological limits for BADs (биологически активные добавки). TPC limit 5×10⁴ CFU/g; yeast and mould: ≤100 CFU/g.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: FDA Ghana Maximum Limits for Contaminants in Food
allowable_limits.notes: Ghana struggles with aflatoxin contamination in domestic groundnuts. FDA-Ghana enforces limits at processing facilities. PACA (Programme for Aflatoxin Control in Africa) involvement.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: Tanzania Food Safety Standards — TFDA/TBS (Tanzania Bureau of Standards)
allowable_limits.notes: Tanzania contaminant limits generally follow Codex. TBS (Tanzania Bureau of Standards) issues national standards. EAC harmonisation will progressively align member state limits.
Morocco's food additive limits largely follow EU Regulation 1333/2008 due to EU Association Agreement. Stricter than Codex for some applications.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: GSO/SASO Nutrient Reference Values — Gulf Standards
allowable_limits.notes: GCC countries use Gulf/Saudi DRVs. Vitamin C NRV: 80 mg/day (aligns with EU NRV for this nutrient).

labeling_requirements.regulatory_basis: TR TS 022/2011 (EAEU Technical Regulation on Food Labelling); Federal Law 29-FZ; GOST R standards
mandatory_fields: Состав (Ingredient list — descending order in Russian)
Наименование и местонахождение изготовителя/уполномоченного лица (Manufacturer or authorised entity in Russia/EAEU)
Знак обращения на рынке ЕС или ЕАЭС (EAEU conformity mark — where applicable)
State Registration Number for BAD supplements (СГР номер)

nutrition_declaration.format: Per 100g/100mL. Energy in both kcal AND kJ. % NRV based on EAEU NRVs (TR TS 022/2011 Annex). Cholesterol: declare if cholesterol claim made.
nutrition_declaration.nrv_reference: TR TS 022/2011 Annex 2 — Nutrient Reference Values (EAEU)
nutrition_declaration.note: EAEU NRVs differ from EU in some nutrients. Russia labels require both kcal and kJ (unlike US which uses only kcal).

allergen_rules.declaration_method: Bold in ingredient list AND 'Содержит:' (Contains:) statement.

weights_measures.weight_units: SI metric units (г, кг, мл, л) mandatory. Use Cyrillic abbreviations.
weights_measures.regulatory_basis: Federal Law on Ensuring Uniformity of Measurements; TR TS 022/2011

language_requirements.mandatory_language: Russian (Cyrillic script) mandatory for all required declarations
language_requirements.eaeu_note: For EAEU (Belarus, Kazakhstan), the state language of each country must also appear. For Russia, Russian only is sufficient.

prohibited_claims: Medicinal claims on food products without registration as pharmaceutical
Claims that products replace prescribed medication

claim_rules.organic: EAEU Organic Production TR EAEU 040/2016 certification

special_requirements: CYRILLIC SCRIPT: all mandatory label text must be in Russian Cyrillic — Latin transliteration insufficient
EAEU conformity mark (EAC — Евразийское соответствие) required where applicable
State Registration Number (СГР) mandatory on label for all BADs (dietary supplements)
GM labeling: mandatory if GMO content >0.9% threshold (stricter than some markets — must state specific GMO)
Irradiated foods: must declare irradiation treatment
For EAEU trade: single label can cover Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan
labeling_requirements.enforcement_notes: Rospotrebnadzor conducts regular market surveillance including Cyrillic label compliance. Non-compliant imports rejected at Russian customs. EAEU conformity declaration or certificate required for products covered by EAEU technical regulations. Western sanctions (post-2022) may affect distribution channels.

labeling_requirements.regulatory_basis: EU Regulation 1169/2011 (FIC) — directly applicable; Polish Food Safety Act 2006
labeling_requirements.competent_authority: GIS (Chief Sanitary Inspectorate); UOKiK (Office of Competition and Consumer Protection) for advertising
mandatory_fields: Data minimalnej trwałości or data ważności (Best before / use by)
Podmiot odpowiedzialny (Responsible FBO name and address in EU)
Kraj lub miejsce pochodzenia (Country of origin — for specified categories)
Sposób użycia (Instructions for use — where needed)
Informacja o wartości odżywczej (Nutrition declaration — mandatory)

mandatory_nutrients: Kwasy tłuszczowe nasycone Saturated fatty acids (g)
Sól Salt (g) — note: SALT not sodium
nutrition_declaration.format: Per 100g/100mL mandatory. Energy in kJ AND kcal. SALT (not sodium) per EU FIC — conversion: salt = sodium × 2.5. % NRV based on EU Regulation 1169/2011 Annex XIII. Front-of-pack Nutri-Score voluntarily used in Poland.
nutrition_declaration.salt_not_sodium: EU FIC requires declaration as SALT (not sodium). Salt = Na × 2.5.

top_allergens: Dwutlenek siarki i siarczany (SO₂ and sulphites >10mg/kg)
allergen_rules.declaration_method: Typographic emphasis (bold) in ingredient list. 'Zawiera:' (Contains:) statement recommended.

weights_measures.net_weight_position: Same field of vision as product name where practicable

language_requirements.mandatory_language: Polish (język polski) for all mandatory declarations
language_requirements.eu_note: Pan-EU products may add Polish to multi-language pack — minimum all 14 EU mandatory particulars in Polish

prohibited_claims: Health claims not on EU Authorised Health Claims Register

claim_rules.organic: EU organic certification (Euroleaf); Polish BIOCOSMETICS or equivalent certification

special_requirements: Poland is an EU member — EU Regulation 1169/2011 (FIC) applies directly
Nutri-Score front-of-pack scheme is growing in Poland — voluntary but retailers may request
Ban on palm oil as 'vegetable oil' — must declare 'palm oil' by name
Country of origin mandatory for: unprocessed meat (beef, pork, sheep, goat, poultry), fresh fruit/vegetables, honey, olive oil, wine, fish
Batch lot marking required per EU Directive 2011/91/EU
E-labels (QR codes for additional information) increasingly used — EU FIC allows supplementary info via QR for all products; mandatory extension proposed
labeling_requirements.enforcement_notes: GIS (Chief Sanitary Inspectorate) and IJHARS (Inspection of Agriculture and Food Quality) enforce food labeling. UOKiK handles advertising compliance. Poland participates in RASFF and EU coordinated enforcement operations. Strong consumer awareness — Polish courts have ruled on label non-compliance.
